current_answer: The commercial case now has stronger evidence of both retained customer value and selective infrastructure persistence. CoreWeave reports a new contract for an older GPU design; a previously used data center supports another customer. That makes automatic obsolescence a weaker explanation, not every terminal value a sound one. Strong payers can protect invoices while maintenance, rent, replacement and financing absorb cash. The best-supported answer remains a real expansion with uneven, sometimes demanding return expectations—not a fictitious economy or a verdict that every AI-related share is a bubble. What the continuation evidence changes.
summary: Real paid demand. Providers can retain value. Selected older capacity can earn again. The harder question is how much net value reaches each investment and ownership claim.
uncertainty: For continuation, obtain the actual A100 term, deployment age and net service economics, plus Austin’s billed-to-collected fees and cash costs. Compare a documented refit with the best feasible continued use rather than assuming every expired contract requires a new generation. Decisive observations and their limits.
freshness_note: Research evidence cutoff: 29 September 2026, a retrieval-day boundary, not a complete end-of-day snapshot. The Austin calculation anchor is 31 March 2025; publication on 1 October is not a new subject refresh.
